Treatment consists of headworks including a manual bar screen and a lift pump station, three lined ponds connected in series (Ponds 1, 2, and 3), each with two aeration units for aerated stabilization, and contact chlorination using sodium hypochlorite followed by dechlorination using sodium bisulfite.
Accumulated biosolids are dredged from the lagoons and from the chlorination chamber and disposed of on drying beds.
Dried solids are analyzed prior to removal off-site for disposal at a landfill.

A separate groundwater pump station, located adjacent to the influent lift pump station, was designed to lower the water level under and around the aeration basins to prevent the liner from “pop” up due to infiltrating water when a basin is being emptied for cleaning or maintenance.

The Discharger indicated in the Report of Waste Discharge submitted on November 7, 2024, that there are planned improvements at the Facility during the upcoming permit term including rehabilitation of the wastewater treatment plant facilities (i.e., liner for ponds, disinfection system, and valves), construction of evaporation/ infiltration ponds to phase out the NPDES discharge and convert to a Waste Discharge Requirements permit for onsite discharge to land.
